mechanism.why: web/index.html hardcodes class="lens on" on #lens-city-manager, shell.css shows on .lens.on and hides on .lens, and the only script in the document is type=module and therefore deferred by definition. So the parser paints Overview from the static document, and applyLens() moves the .on class only after the whole document has parsed. Every deep link paints Overview first.

shapeChosen.form: an inline classless <script> in <head> that resolves the query string and stamps attributes on the ROOT element, plus attribute-keyed visibility enumerations in web/shell.css. Visibility is decided by the parser before first paint, so the flash is structurally impossible rather than merely faster.
attributesStamped: data-surface = the resolved SECTION id, e.g. lens-finance or work-connections
data-tab = the resolved Development-services tab id, empty when the lens is not development-services
data-atab = the resolved Assets tab id, empty when the work view is not assets

namingDivergenceFromA072_flagged.a072Said: stamps data-lens on the root element
namingDivergenceFromA072_flagged.why: data-lens ALREADY EXISTS in this document, on the nav anchors, carrying a different vocabulary - the bare lens id (finance), where the root needs the section id (lens-finance). app.js reads el.dataset.lens on .navitem. Putting a second value vocabulary under one attribute name is the naming trap, and html[data-lens] would also start matching any future querySelectorAll for [data-lens]. data-surface is the product's own word for these fifteen things (the G-88 surface inventory calls them fifteen surfaces) and it stays true after applyLens writes it too.

shapeChosen.gateIsPRESENCEnotVALUE: the hide rules are html[data-surface] .lens, html[data-tab] .ds-tab and html[data-atab] .assets-tab. With scripting off no attribute is ever stamped, none of the three hide rules applies, and the static class="lens on" governs exactly as it does today. The JS-disabled reachability is therefore unchanged by construction, and it is measured rather than assumed.

specificityComputedNotAssumed.hideSelector: html[data-surface] .lens is (0,2,1) - one attribute plus one class in b, one type selector (html) in c
specificityComputedNotAssumed.hideBeatsStaticOn: (0,2,1) beats (0,2,0) on the b/c comparison, and it does not depend on source order
specificityComputedNotAssumed.showBeatsHide: (1,1,1) beats (0,2,1) - an id outranks any number of classes and attributes
specificityComputedNotAssumed.onlyOtherDisplayRuleThatCanReachALensSec: [hidden]:not([hidden="until-found" i]) { display: none !important; } at shell.css:51. It carries !important so it outranks everything, and it applies only to an element carrying the hidden attribute. No .lens section carries hidden, so it does not apply; if one ever did, hiding is the intent.
specificityComputedNotAssumed.howThisWasEstablished: not by reading - by parsing all 230 rules in web/shell.css, taking the 68 that declare display, and filtering to those whose rightmost compound could match an element with tag section, id in the fifteen, and classes drawn from lens/on/roster-lens. Exactly two survive: .lens and .lens.on. No @media, @supports or @container block in the file mentions lens at all.
specificityComputedNotAssumed.noImportantAdded: src/hidden-rule.test.mjs check 4 forbids any OTHER rule declaring display with !important. None of my rules uses !important; specificity alone carries them.

enumerationCount.countingRule: one show selector per addressable panel: fifteen section.lens elements in web/index.html, six DS_TABS and three ASSET_TABS in src/staff-review.mjs. Three hide rules, one per axis.
enumerationCount.whatKeepsItInStepWithTheSectionList: src/first-paint.test.mjs asserts a THREE-WAY set equality per axis: the ids derived from src/staff-review.mjs (lens- prefixed ALL_LENS_IDS union work- prefixed WORK_IDS), the ids of the .lens sections parsed out of web/index.html, and the ids enumerated in the show rule parsed out of web/shell.css. Adding a sixteenth section without its selector fails the suite instead of shipping a screen that paints blank. This is a mechanized control, not a note asking a future author to remember (DEV_PROCESS rule 0).
enumerationCount.oneRuleAlternativeConsideredAndRejected: the :target pseudo-class keys one CSS rule off the URL fragment and would need no enumeration, but it requires /#lens-finance rather than /?lens=finance. That changes the URL contract, breaks every existing deep link and every href in the nav, and the head script cannot set a fragment without navigating. Rejected on cost, and named here so a reader can see it was considered.

applyLensMustNotGoDead.risk: if the attribute governs visibility and applyLens() only toggles .on, the class becomes decorative and any future JS-driven lens change silently does nothing.
applyLensMustNotGoDead.decision: applyLens() becomes the single writer of the same three root attributes, alongside the class toggles it already does. Class and attribute can then never disagree, and both remain live. The head script is a pre-paint copy of the same computation, not a competing mechanism.
applyLensMustNotGoDead.assertedBy: src/first-paint.test.mjs asserts app.js writes all three attributes inside applyLens, and asserts the values it writes are derived from the same staffLens fields the class toggles use.

pairedControlAndItsDivergenceTest.theTwoImplementations: resolveStaffLensQuery() in src/staff-review.mjs, and the inline head script in web/index.html which cannot import it (an import makes the script a module, and a module is deferred, which is the whole defect).
pairedControlAndItsDivergenceTest.control: src/first-paint.test.mjs compares them three ways rather than by two careful edits (DEV_PROCESS 2.4). BEHAVIOURAL: for every id the module accepts, the head script executed in a node:vm sandbox must stamp the matching surface. TEXTUAL: the id arrays and the fallback literal are extracted from the inline script source and asserted set-equal to ALL_LENS_IDS, WORK_IDS and CITY_MANAGER_LENS imported from the module. CROSS-CHECK: every id in the textual set behaves as accepted and every id outside it behaves as rejected, which proves the textual extraction actually describes the script rather than describing a regex.
pairedControlAndItsDivergenceTest.provenToFire: a second arm in the SAME test feeds a MUTATED copy of the script text - one id deleted, one id added - and asserts the comparison returns the exact expected mismatch. Both arms in one test, per the G-88 item 3 precedent that a clean arm and an injected arm in different tests let an unrun check and a passing check look alike.

instrument1_howItWillBeMadeToFail.file: src/first-paint.test.mjs, in the suite, exit-bounded, no browser
instrument1_howItWillBeMadeToFail.computes: the FIRST-PAINT visible set. Parses web/index.html for every section.lens with its id, classes and attributes; parses web/shell.css into rules with their at-rule context; executes ONLY the inline head script in a node:vm sandbox with a stub location.search and a stub documentElement, because at first paint the module has not run; then resolves display for each section by real cascade order - importance, then specificity, then source order.
instrument1_howItWillBeMadeToFail.failLoudNotFailQuiet: the resolver refuses to guess. A display rule whose rightmost compound could match a .lens section but whose ancestor part references anything other than the root, or which sits inside a conditional group rule, or which uses selector syntax outside the modeled subset, THROWS naming the selector. An instrument that silently returns no-match on syntax it does not understand is the defect class this program hunts (DEV_PROCESS 4.3).
instrument1_howItWillBeMadeToFail.theFailingArm: test-fixtures/g89-pre-fix/index.html and test-fixtures/g89-pre-fix/shell.css are byte copies of web/index.html and web/shell.css at 6a4580d, taken BEFORE any edit. The same pure function runs against the fixture in the SAME test and is asserted to return {lens-city-manager} where {lens-finance} was expected. Not git stash: a fixture survives a clone and a stash does not. The fixture is frozen by a sha256 pin in the test, so a helpful refresh fails loudly.
instrument1_howItWillBeMadeToFail.fixtureHousing: test-fixtures/ at the repo root, deliberately not under src/ or web/. shape.test.mjs walks exactly src and web for .mjs/.js/.html, so a frozen copy placed there would be judged forever by gates it can never be edited to satisfy - a permanently-red gate is a dead gate (DEV_PROCESS 2.0). The Dockerfile COPYs only src and web, so the fixture also never enters the image.
